speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: How long have you had this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg, and has it changed in size or appearance since it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of ant bite is intriguing, but given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent steroid use for uveitis, could you describe the current appearance of the ulcer—specifically, does it have a raised, rolled border or a "punched-out" center? Also, has it produced any discharge?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential, Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide high-resolution clinical photos of the lesion showing the borders and base.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (Requested tests ESR and CRP not present in data; CBC shows WBC: Normal, Hemoglobin: Normal, Platelets: Normal)

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Given the "punched-out" ulcer with a purplish, irregular border and a history of Crohn's disease and recent steroid use, the clinical picture strongly suggests Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than cellulitis or an infected ant bite. Please confirm if the lesion has increased in size despite any prior treatment attempts.
